name: VALL-E-X
description: Open-source implementation of Microsoft's VALL-E X zero-shot cross-lingual TTS and voice cloning (Plachtaa/VALL-E-X). Clones a voice from a 3-10s reference clip (with optional Whisper auto-transcription) and synthesizes English/Chinese/Japanese speech in that timbre. Self-hosted via a Gradio web UI launched with `python -X utf8 launch-ui.py`, default http://localhost:7860/. Archived upstream (read-only Nov 2025) at ~7.9k stars; HF-Space clones and forks run the identical Gradio surface.
auth_notes: No authentication in launch-ui.py — Gradio launch() is called without the auth= tuple, leaving the voice-cloning UI, reference-audio upload/recording, and prompt-preset management fully open on port 7860. No key gates synthesis. Operators must bind localhost or reverse-proxy; the README simply directs users to the local Gradio URL. Gradio share=True (gradio.live) tunnels are a common accidental public-exposure path for the demo.

shodan_dorks.rationale: Gradio's inline window.gradio_config JSON blob is the http.html-visible signal past the SPA shell; broad Gradio-on-7860 net to narrow by VALL-E-X labels.
VALL-E / VALL-E-X app title or markdown header rendered into gradio_config on the index page; direct name match for unmodified deployments.
'Make prompt' / 'make prompt from audio' is VALL-E-X's distinctive voice-prompt-creation tab label surfaced in gradio_config; separates it from generic Gradio TTS demos.

shodan_dorks.query: port:7860 http.html:"gradio_config" http.html:"infer from prompt" http.html:"accent"
shodan_dorks.rationale: 'infer from prompt' plus the accent/language selector labels co-occur only in the VALL-E-X UI; very high precision.
Whisper auto-transcription toggle presence indicates the full-featured build; use to segment complete deployments for targeted enumeration.

known_vulns: No built-in auth — unauthenticated access to zero-shot voice cloning, reference-audio upload/recording, and synthesis on port 7860
Gradio file-component path-traversal / arbitrary-file-read CVEs (CVE-2024-1561 and related) apply to exposed launch-ui.py instances on vulnerable Gradio versions
Zero-shot cloning from a 3-10s clip — trivially low barrier to impersonation; open UI = turnkey deepfake generator
Unrestricted audio upload with no size/MIME validation — GPU/VRAM and disk DoS
Saved voice prompts (.npz) accumulate on the host; exposed customs/ directory disclosure leaks previously-cloned voices
share=True gradio.live tunnels publish the UI publicly with no auth
gradio_config / /config disclose component structure and referenced local model/prompt filenames
risk_notes: Primary attack vectors: (1) Turnkey non-consensual voice cloning — a few seconds of a target's audio plus the open UI yields cross-lingual impersonation speech; a direct vishing/fraud, disinformation, and harassment surface. (2) Cloned-voice-prompt exfiltration — the customs/ prompt cache holds .npz voice embeddings of every voice the operator (or prior visitors) cloned; disclosure leaks reusable identity artifacts. (3) Compute theft — open GPU synthesis automatable via /run/predict at operator cost. (4) Gradio-version file read — chaining a Gradio path-traversal CVE yields arbitrary file read of weights, prompts, and adjacent secrets. (5) share-tunnel exposure bypasses network controls the operator assumed were in place.
deployment_notes: CUDA GPU host (min ~6GB VRAM, Python 3.10). The single network surface is the launch-ui.py Gradio app on :7860. SHODAN VISIBILITY CAVEAT: Gradio SPA — rendered UI text is JS-only and http.html-blind; pivot on the inline window.gradio_config JSON blob (indexed by Shodan/Censys) plus VALL-E-X-specific tab labels ('make prompt', 'infer from prompt'). Censys services.http.response.html_title 'Gradio' + body substring match on gradio_config + 'VALL-E' is the reliable cross-source method. Upstream archived; HF-Space redeployments and forks constitute the live population.
